author: ammaaya
quote:
I only became excited for this game after the extended look on Netflix and the ensuing promotional interviews following it which gave the impression that that not only would this entry of the GTA franchise would be a big step up from its usually lackluster writing quality but also feature almost Bioware-esque RPG elements and player choice and agency.

Now that the game is actually here, after all the fan excitement and fan perception that was a result of that marketing, and been here long enough to experience the whole story... it's safe to say that the marketing of this game was downright deceptive. 

The saddest part is that much of this was an unforced error.

Rockstar knew that they could've marketed pretty much anything and still made record profits, they could have marketed yet another simple story-on-rails which writing that isn't trying to get an award anytime soon— something that is to be expected from all previous GTA entries —and yet, Rockstar insisted, almost duplicitously, that this entry was so so "different" and meant to be an almost wholly new experience.

Well, as someone who was originally unexcited for this game because I assumed it would be the same old same old generic story with the shallowest of RPG elements and a flimsy veneer of player choice and agency, I wish I had never changed my original assumption.

I shouldn't have gotten taken in by the marketing hype. I really thought this one was gonna be different. The only "difference" is the main characters are just as shallowly written as usual, but in a specific way that feels very dated to the era that this game was originally developed in, which is already a few years ago at this point, mind you!

author: ammaaya
quote:
Sims 4 is already infamous for being devoid of gameplay at launch and for an insidious cashgrab payment model, so naturally the Sims team and EA decided to release a $20 ad for a new section of Disneyland that's also completely empty of gameplay outside of pointing and clicking on objects and entering 2 buildings (the rest are shells/non-enterable)

What's worse is that this comes on the heels of the Sims team being under fire from fans for not having adequate dark skintones even 6 years after release, and after John Boyega was interviewed detailing the racism within the production of the sequel SW trilogy and how he was pushed out of the leading male role. And what did the Sims do after this? They released a pack that advertised the characters from the sequel trilogy... but only the white ones, Rey & Kylo!

Now we have a collab between 2 franchises famous for giving the middle finger towards black fans, that really only serves to give the white girls their fave Star Wars angry **** boyfriend as a Sim to add to their families. Not only that but in true Sims 4 fashion, it is completely devoid of deeper-than-surface-level gameplay and only provides some set dressing, some build objects, and new clothes just like every other damn pack in the Sims 4.

The only positive is that it seems that the fanbase is really starting to realize that enough is enough with this garbage treatment from the dev team, it's insulting, and we deserve better from the life simulation genre.
game_title: The Sims 4: Star Wars - Journey to Batuu
